title: API Sheriff endpoints/*.yaml
description: JSON Schema for a single endpoint file under endpoints/*.yaml. Mirrors doc/configuration.adoc field-for-field. Endpoint-id uniqueness across files, upstream_defaults wholesale-replacement, allowed_methods no-inheritance semantics, and anchor membership/namespace agreement are enforced in code, not schema. Unknown keys are rejected at every object level (additionalProperties: false).

token_relay.description: Whether a require: session route relays the session's access token to the upstream as Authorization: Bearer. Defaults to true. With false the session is still resolved, refreshed and required, but no Authorization header is sent upstream. Acts only on require: session; it has no effect on bearer or none routes. Combining false with a forward.headers_allow that names Authorization is refused at boot (enforced in code). The auth block is replaced wholesale through the route -> endpoint -> anchor cascade, so the key is inherited only together with the rest of the block.

id.description: Unique endpoint name (mandatory). Uniqueness across all endpoint files is enforced in code.

enabled.description: Whether this endpoint is active. Defaults to true. Overridable in-file via a ${VAR:-default} placeholder on the value.

base_url.description: Topology alias resolved from topology.properties. Never a concrete host. Mandatory exactly when the endpoint carries a proxy route (a route declaring neither asset nor redirect); an endpoint serving only asset and/or redirect routes may omit it. The conditional mandatoriness is enforced in code.

anchor.description: Optional default anchor name for this endpoint's routes; a route may override it. Membership/namespace agreement is enforced in code.

auth.description: Optional default auth posture for the routes. When omitted, an anchor-provided auth (or a route-level auth) must supply the effective posture; conditional mandatoriness is enforced in code.

scopes.description: Optional OIDC scopes this endpoint needs IN ADDITION to the gateway's oidc.scopes. Additive only: the scope set a route of this endpoint needs is oidc.scopes united with this list, so an endpoint can add scopes but never remove one. That one set is requested at a session-route login and checked on a bearer route (403 insufficient_scope when the token lacks a member). Declared on the endpoint, outside auth, so it is not replaced by a route- or anchor-level auth block. Declaring it on an enabled endpoint whose routes all resolve require: none is refused at boot (enforced in code). Each entry must be an RFC 6749 section 3.3 scope-token: one or more printable ASCII characters (0x21-0x7E) excluding the double quote and the backslash, so no space, no control character and no non-ASCII; a malformed name is refused at load. The pattern terminates with a negative lookahead rather than '$', because '$' also matches before a final line terminator.

allowed_methods.description: Optional per-endpoint verb allowlist. REPLACES the global gateway.allowed_methods (and any anchor allowed_methods) wholesale for this endpoint (no inheritance). TRACE and CONNECT are excluded from the enum.

upstream_defaults.description: Optional endpoint-level retry / not-modified defaults. When present, replaces the global upstream_defaults wholesale for this endpoint.

catalog.description: Optional portal overview entry. A catalog block lists this endpoint on the portal page, active exactly when the endpoint is enabled after placeholder resolution, so ENDPOINT_<ID>_ENABLED toggles the entry together with the routes. Every value is HTML-escaped when rendered.

description.description: Optional one-line description rendered under the title.

entry.description: The link target: an origin-relative absolute path on the gateway's own origin — a single leading '/', no '//', no backslash, no control characters. A scheme, an authority or a scheme-relative '//host' value would turn the portal into an open redirect and is refused; the configuration validator additionally refuses encoded variants at boot, naming the offending endpoint.

order.description: Optional sort key; entries are listed by ascending order, then by title. An entry without order sorts after every entry that declares one.

anchor.description: Optional per-route anchor override; when absent, the endpoint anchor applies. Membership/namespace agreement is enforced in code.

match.description: The route matcher set. Exactly one of path_prefix or path must be declared. Matchers compose with AND semantics.

path_prefix.description: Literal path prefix matched on a segment boundary; the longest prefix wins among prefix routes. Mutually exclusive with path.

path.description: Exact path matched by an un-normalized string comparison against the canonical request path: /a and /a/ are distinct addresses. Exact routes are selected before any prefix route. Mutually exclusive with path_prefix.

forward.description: Per-route forward filter applied INSIDE an already-authorised route (deny-by-default lives at the URL layer, not here). Each dimension - headers, query - resolves exactly one of three modes: a positive-list when *_allow is declared, a negative-list when *_deny is declared, and forward-all when neither is. An absent list is not the same as a declared empty one: query_allow: [] is a positive-list admitting nothing, while an omitted query_allow is forward-all. Declaring both lists for one dimension is refused at boot in code, not by this schema: additionalProperties: false bounds the key set, but a mutual exclusion between two optional keys is cross-cutting and belongs with the other post-binding rules.

headers_allow.description: Positive-list of forwardable request-header names. Naming Authorization here is the ONLY way an inbound Authorization is re-admitted past the gateway-owned never-forward set; Cookie is absolute and no list re-admits it. Mutually exclusive with headers_deny (enforced in code).

headers_deny.description: Negative-list of withheld request-header names; every other client header crosses EXCEPT the gateway-owned never-forward set, which applies under every mode (Cookie, an inbound Authorization, the hop-by-hop, framing and provenance names). The gateway-understood protocol headers cross without being named, and a name listed here withholds them too. Mutually exclusive with headers_allow (enforced in code).

query_allow.description: Positive-list of forwardable query-parameter names. Mutually exclusive with query_deny (enforced in code).

query_deny.description: Negative-list of withheld query-parameter names; every other client parameter crosses. Mutually exclusive with query_allow (enforced in code).

path.description: Upstream path appended to the topology alias base path, joined on exactly one slash (ADR-0004 Amendment A2). The request remainder after the match key follows it. Omitted or blank keeps the alias base path.

rewrite_location.description: Whether an upstream Location response header pointing inside this route's upstream is mapped back onto the gateway. A relative path or an absolute URI whose scheme, host and effective port equal the route upstream, and whose path equals the effective upstream base path or continues it on a segment boundary, is rewritten to the route's match key plus the remainder, emitted as a gateway-relative path; query and fragment are kept verbatim. Foreign origins, scheme-relative //host values, unparseable values and paths outside the base path are relayed unchanged. Defaults to false (Location relayed unchanged). Valid on http and graphql routes only; refused on grpc and websocket routes (enforced in code).

asset.description: Optional asset terminal action (ADR-0014). Serves static content through the gateway-owned response envelope instead of proxying. asset and redirect are the two explicit terminal actions and are mutually exclusive; a route declaring neither proxies, to the endpoint base_url unless a route-level upstream block overrides it (enforced in code).

source.description: The asset content source discriminator: a local directory / volume mount, or a secondary origin reached through the SSRF-controlled data plane.

directory.description: The local directory root for source: directory. Served through path confinement; no classpath-embedded resources.

upstream.description: The topology alias of the secondary origin for source: upstream.

index.description: Directory index file name for source: directory (e.g. index.html). A request addressing a directory - the empty sub-path, a sub-path ending with /, or an existing directory - is answered with this file from that directory, served through the same path confinement as any other asset; a directory without the file is a 404. A single file-name segment: no /, no backslash, no .., no control characters, not empty. Refused on source: upstream (enforced in code).

fallback.description: Single-page-application fallback file name for source: directory. A request whose target does not exist and whose last path segment carries no dot extension is answered with this root-level file, served through the same path confinement as any other asset; an unknown path with an extension (e.g. /app.js) stays a 404. A single file-name segment: no /, no backslash, no .., no control characters, not empty. Refused on source: upstream (enforced in code).

redirect.description: Optional redirect terminal action (ADR-0014 Amendment A1). The gateway answers the request itself with the configured status and Location, without contacting any upstream. redirect and asset are the two explicit terminal actions and are mutually exclusive; a route declaring neither proxies, to the endpoint base_url unless a route-level upstream block overrides it. The open-redirect review of location and the protocol restriction are enforced in code.

location.description: The Location value, written verbatim (never context-path-prefixed, no request placeholders). Without allow_external it must be a single-slash gateway path free of backslashes, encoded slashes, dot-segments and control characters.

status.description: The redirect status. Mandatory rather than defaulted: 301 and 308 are cached by browsers, so permanence must be an explicit operator choice.

keep_query.description: Whether the raw inbound query string is appended to location (joined with ? or &). Defaults to false. Same-origin only: combining it with allow_external fails the boot, because the inbound query is attacker-supplied and would be handed to the foreign origin.

allow_external.description: Whether location may be an absolute http/https URI on another origin. Defaults to false; opting in emits a boot warning and cannot be combined with keep_query.

rate_limit.description: Reserved; the rate-limit feature is deferred. Accepted and ignored.

websocket.description: The per-route WebSocket block, valid only on a protocol: websocket route (ADR-0015). allowed_origins is a fail-closed, deny-by-default allowlist of exact-match Origin strings (scheme + host + port, no wildcards); an absent or empty allowlist on a bearer WebSocket route rejects the upgrade at boot. idle_timeout_seconds bounds an established relay and defaults to 300 when absent. The bearer-route allowlist mandatoriness, wildcard rejection, and positive-timeout rules are enforced in code, not schema.

allowed_origins.description: Exact-match, case-insensitive-host Origin allowlist (scheme + host + port). No wildcards.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Per-route idle timeout in seconds; a positive integer. Defaults to 300 when omitted.
